images.title: What counts as proof someone will pay
images.alt: Comparison of validation evidence: pre-orders, paid pilots and deposits count, while compliments and survey answers don't.
images.caption: Evidence that costs the person nothing tells you little about whether they'll pay.

images.title: Fixing the monetization
images.alt: Steps for months seven to ten: see which offer sells, find where people drop off, note unmet requests, test a higher price.
images.caption: Real buying data often disagrees with the original plan, so let it steer the offer.

items.title: See which offer gets bought
items.text: Use the data from people who are now arriving.

items.title: Find where people drop off
items.text: Look for the point where interested visitors stop.

items.title: Note what customers ask for
items.text: List requests for things you don't sell yet.

items.title: Test a higher price
items.text: Underpricing is the usual mistake at this stage.

items.title: Settle on one offer
items.text: Done means strangers have bought it more than once.

images.after: How to tell whether to keep going
images.title: Reading a flat line at review time
images.alt: Decision for a flat result at a review point: after a stage done properly, change something; after a rushed stage, go back.
images.caption: Review at months 3, 6 and 12, and compare against your own earlier numbers.

data.question: Your numbers are flat at a review point. How did the last stage go?

branches.result: Change the idea, the audience or the channel.
